Hi Lina — thanks for sending this over and for the clear list. I’m looping in Karthik (our deployment lead) and will coordinate legal input offline. Quick answers and next steps: 

1) Playbook: we have a short internal playbook (attached) that covers snapshot cadence, signing and hashing of artifacts, key custody, and a two-party witness flow for handover. I can convert to a customer-facing 2-page version.

2) Witness / escrow alternatives: we support three patterns:
   - Sealed snapshot deposit with third‑party custodian (escrow-lite)
   - Witnessed on-prem snapshot where a customer rep and a Redwood steward sign a transfer manifest (no third party)
   - Remote cryptographic proof of possession + HSM-backed key escrow for emergency access

3) Contract language: we generally propose an Order Form exhibit that specifies the chosen pathway (e.g., Exhibit A: Snapshot & Handover) and a short MSA clause that limits access to the narrow forensic/termination scenarios with defined notice and audit windows.

Requests: could you tell me which of the three patterns MedTech prefers? Also, please indicate whether you need Redwood personnel to be listed explicitly in the MSA (we can do a role-based clause instead). If you’re OK we’ll circulate a concise playbook + proposed redline exhibit for review by EOD Thursday.

Thanks —

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priv deploy - evidence & chain-of-custody playbook request

Priyom / Karthik — quick legal read and suggested approach. I’ve attached a draft of recommended redlines and a short sample Exhibit A. Highlights:

- License scope: avoid model residency language that implies transfer of IP. Keep it limited to "temporary possession of cryptographic snapshots for the limited purpose of evidence/forensics under defined scenarios."
- Access triggers: narrow to (a) customer-requested forensic exercise, (b) termination where customer demonstrates inability to access snapshots, or (c) court order. Avoid broad business-continuity clauses that could be interpreted as a general right to run customer workloads.
- Witness language: we can accept a two-party witnessed handover in lieu of a third‑party custodian for customers in the same legal jurisdiction. For highly regulated customers, propose an escrow‑style sealed deposit with a named custodian (sample clause included).
- Audit & retention: define retention windows (e.g., snapshots retained encrypted for 90 days post-termination unless otherwise agreed) and a narrow audit scope for access logs.

I added inline comments in redline_suggestions.docx with suggested MSA/Order Form wording. Biggest legal asks from our side: explicit limitation of access to specific roles and an indemnity carve-out for misuse of customer-supplied keys.

If MedTech prefers the escrow-lite custodian option, we’ll need to identify acceptable custodians and add a short schedule to the Order Form. If they want a witnessed transfer, we can provide a Witness Acceptance Form and template manifest.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call with MedTech legal to run through the clauses — suggest Wed morning if that works for everyone.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Attachment: redline_suggestions.docx (DOCX, 24 KB)
